profile_text.body:
The Allen Institute for AI (also known as Ai2) is a nonprofit research organization founded in 2014 by Paul Allen and headquartered in Seattle, WA. Led by Ali Farhadi, the institute conducts research and engineering aimed at advancing artificial intelligence, with stated priorities around open, collaborative, and inclusive principles. The organization describes its work as spanning foundational AI research as well as applied domains including climate science, agriculture and food security, wildfire management, and wildlife protection.

Ai2's AI work centers on two tracked products. OLMo is an open-source large language model developed with fully open training data and an emphasis on research transparency, consistent with the institute's nonprofit mission. Semantic Scholar is an AI-powered academic search tool offering paper summaries and citation graphs, oriented toward the research community. The site notes partnerships with the University of Washington's Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science and Engineering, the National Science Foundation on an Open Multimodal AI Infrastructure project, and Google Cloud to support model development and scientific AI platforms.

The held facts record no litigation and no MCP server presence. The institute is classified as a nonprofit research lab, verified as of August 2026.
